LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard, well-formed package definition for ulauncher. The `source` array downloads a release tarball from the project's own official GitHub releases page (`https://github.com/Ulauncher/Ulauncher/releases/download/${pkgver}/ulauncher_${pkgver}.tar.gz`), which is entirely consistent with standard AUR packaging practice for upstream-released software. The download is pinned with a SHA256 checksum (`084959f0cc88b78ce6ee34c1122235067fe3323cf5e5a11d1348521380475322`).

There is no `pkgver()` function, and the top-level/global scope of the PKGBUILD contains only variable assignments with no command substitutions, `eval`, encoded blobs, or network operations. The `build()` and `package()` functions exist but will not execute under `--nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, so their contents (`python setup.py build/install`, cache cleanup with `rm -rf`/`find`) are out of scope for this gate and will be reviewed during the full audit.

No malicious behavior is present at the source-fetching/PKGBUILD-sourcing stage.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard PKGBUILD with pinned upstream source; no malicious sourcing behavior.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard, well-formed packaging script for the ulauncher application launcher. The source is downloaded from the official upstream GitHub releases page (`https://github.com/Ulauncher/Ulauncher/releases/download/${pkgver}/...`), which is the expected and trusted source for this package. A SHA256 checksum is provided and pinned, allowing verification of the downloaded tarball.

The build process follows standard Python packaging practices: `python setup.py build` followed by `python setup.py install --root="$pkgdir" --optimize=1 --skip-build`. The use of `getconf PATH` to obtain a clean PATH is a recognized hardening practice that prevents build-time influence from the user's environment. Setting `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` is a standard reproducibility measure for Python packages. The cleanup of `__pycache__` directories and the `rm -rf` of certain preference subdirectories (`no*,src,bow*,gul*,pack*`) are routine package hygiene operations to strip dev artifacts from the installed tree.

All dependencies are standard Arch Linux system packages (GTK3, webkit2gtk, python bindings, etc.) consistent with the application's stated purpose as a Linux application launcher. There are no suspicious network requests, no obfuscated code, no dangerous commands like `eval`, no unexpected file operations outside `$pkgdir`, and no evidence of supply-chain injection.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard PKGBUILD for ulauncher with pinned checksum and clean build practices.</summary>
</security_assessment>

There are no network requests, no downloads, no obfuscation, and no execution of privileged or dangerous commands. This is routine AUR packaging practice for applications that ship a user-level systemd service.
